name: Store and site operations (the trading floor's operating day)
one_line: The record a TRADING OPERATION keeps of RUNNING ONE SITE through one operating day or shift cycle: labour hours planned against forecast covers or sales, the opening and closing of the trading floor itself, the shift handover of trading-floor state, a brand or mystery-shopper standards walk of the selling space, and a reactive call raised from the floor during service. Its anchor is the SITE OPERATING DAY - bounded by open and close of that selling space - not a till session, not a stock count, not a licence file, and not the occupier's multi-month facilities calendar. It is the OPERATOR's side only. A PLACEHOLDER TEMPLATE on the fieldless retail_hospitality schema: it declares NO field rows (PR-6, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, D1 as narrowed) and recommends NO serialised dimension_order, so its difference from the family default is held as prose.

deterministic: PRECONDITION on every entry below: each is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The `retail_hospitality` schema declares no field rows, so nothing here writes a domain fact. Detection exists so the material is recognised, held under this row's privacy posture, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

A LABOUR-AGAINST-FORECAST structure - this row's strongest and most decisive signal, and the discriminator the parent schema already named as NJ-RH-1. A rota or labour plan with names or roles down one axis and days or shifts across the other, PLUS a FORECAST COVERS, FORECAST SALES, SALES-PER-LABOUR-HOUR, LABOUR-PERCENTAGE or LABOUR-COST-AGAINST-SALES column in the same sheet. The forecast-trade column is what fires; without it the bare rota is undecidable against `hr` and this row must not claim it alone.

A TRADING-FLOOR OPENING-AND-CLOSING CHECK structure. A dated checklist keyed to a named site, store or unit, whose rows name trading-floor acts - float set or counted into the safe, tills opened or closed, alarm set or unset, shutters, lights, visual merchandising or brand-standards walk, fire-exit check as a daily tick, keys signed out - with an INITIAL or signature slot per row or per section. The discriminator against `retail_hospitality.food-safety` is the VOCABULARY OF THE CHECK: probe, core temperature, fridge, freezer, use-by and cleaning-schedule rows decide for food-safety; float, till, alarm, shutter and visual-merch rows decide for this row. The discriminator against `business_operations.facilities-workplace` is TIME SHAPE: a multi-month planned-maintenance or statutory-inspection calendar decides for facilities; a same-day open/close diary decides for this row.

A BRAND-STANDARDS OR MYSTERY-SHOPPER VISIT structure. A scorecard or visit report keyed to one store and one visit date, with scored sections over the SELLING SPACE (greeting, queue, merchandising, cleanliness-as-presented-to-guest, brand script) and usually a mystery-shopper or regional-manager producer mark. The discriminator against `business_operations.compliance-audit` is decisive in both directions: that row's anchor is an ASSESSMENT OCCURRENCE with a request-to-evidence-to-finding-to-sign-off chain against a REGULATORY or POLICY CONTROL framework performed by a party structurally distinct from the party assessed; this is a BRAND-OPS score of the trading floor, with no PBC request list and no control-framework citation.

A SHIFT-HANDOVER OF TRADING-FLOOR STATE. A dated note or form naming the outgoing and incoming duty manager or shift lead, carrying a short list of OPEN TRADING CONDITIONS handed across - float status, known till exceptions, guest issues still live, equipment down, deliveries expected - without being a till close and without being a personnel case. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

A TRADING-FLOOR REACTIVE INCIDENT CALL raised DURING SERVICE. A short ticket or email naming a failed fridge, a broken till, a blocked door or a guest-affecting fault, keyed to a site and a trading date, with an urgency mark and often a temporary workaround. The discriminator against `business_operations.facilities-workplace` is that facilities owns the CONTRACTOR SCHEDULE and the planned-maintenance calendar for the same appliance; this row owns the SAME-DAY CALL raised from the floor so trading can continue.

A SITE-DAY PACK ASSEMBLY. A bound or zipped pack whose manifest or contents page lists, for ONE site and ONE period, two or more of: opening/closing checks, a labour plan, a standards visit, a handover log, AND often neighbours' members (Z-reads, food-safety sheets, a licence copy) as CONTAINED items. This row owns THE PACK AS AN ASSEMBLY - its cover, its ordering, the reason the site holds it together. Containment is not ownership of the contained closes or temp logs. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

An email whose labelled subject slot names a rota, an opening check, a closing check, a standards visit, a mystery shop, a shift handover or a site pack AND whose attachment-name slot names a checklist, a scorecard, a labour plan or a pack. The reference-plus-attachment pairing fires; a hospitality-sounding sender domain alone does not.

An archive whose manifest names a site pack, a store-ops export, a week's opening-check scans or a standards-visit batch - read from the manifest alone, because “However, the normal scan should never extract archive contents to the filesystem, because doing so creates security, storage, and side-effect risks.”

Parent-folder context naming a store or unit number, a trading week, opening checks or store ops, treated as a clue that raises plausibility once one of the structures above is already present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this row's ordinary output names STAFF on labour plans and often carries till-exception suspicion and guest-affecting incident prose, so a model step runs under the user's policy and after P7. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

Deciding whether a bare rota is this row's labour-against-forecast plan or `hr`'s workforce schedule. The SPLH / labour-percentage / forecast-covers column decides for this row; contracted hours, absence codes or pay rates decide for hr. Where neither is present, abstain - this is NJ-SO-1 / the parent's NJ-RH-1, not a quiet win.

Separating a TRADING-FLOOR open/close checklist from a FOOD-SAFETY daily diary and from a FACILITIES statutory calendar when the same scanned clipboard sheet mixes rows. Vocabulary of the check decides; mixed sheets are review candidates, not automatic activations.

Separating a BRAND standards visit from a REGULATORY compliance assessment when both score a store. Presence of a PBC request list, a control-framework citation or a findings-and-corrective-action register decides for `business_operations.compliance-audit`; a mystery-shopper or regional brand scorecard without those decides for this row.

Separating a REAL operating record from a FRANCHISE OPERATIONS MANUAL, a training blank, a specimen checklist or a downloaded compliance pack. A blank opening-check sheet and a completed one are the same form with the ticks removed. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”

Unlabelled operational prose: a duty manager's handover scribble, an incident write-up naming a guest and a staff member, a chaser about a failed fridge during dinner service. No header block, and frequently the most sensitive files in the set.

Reading a SCANNED OR PHOTOGRAPHED paper checklist or rota. Handwriting is often the whole content; OCR confidence on initials and ticks is low. “A screenshot is always a screenshot of something—a receipt, application portal, conversation, code problem, document, calendar, or research figure—and without OCR the product sees only an image with a weak filename.”
In every case above, abstention is the required outcome when evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: THE DOCUMENT-TYPE WORDS THEMSELVES - rota, opening checks, closing checks, standards audit, mystery shopper, handover, maintenance call, site pack - standing alone. The parent schema's never-alone list already says a document-type word is a value of a function dimension, and a row resting on one is the schema's default template wearing a name. `Rota.xlsx` with no forecast-trade column is not this row.

A TRADE NAME, STORE NUMBER OR BRAND standing alone - `Camden`, `Store 214`, `The Bell`. Constitutionally never-alone; read across from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”

A STAFF MEMBER'S NAME on a rota or a signature slot. A person's name must never anchor a group and must never become a folder level - “The engine validates that the proposed template does not repeat a parent dimension, create meaningless one-child levels, exceed practical depth limits, use an author or organization merely as a collector, expose protected information, or produce empty branches when tested against the accepted group.”
A DATE, however trading-day-shaped. `2026-03-14.xlsx` is not an operating-day record.

A CLEANING WORD standing alone - clean, deep clean, hygiene. Cleaning-schedule structure with food or probe vocabulary is `retail_hospitality.food-safety`'s; a facilities cleaning contract is `business_operations.facilities-workplace`'s.

A MAINTENANCE OR CONTRACTOR WORD standing alone. A fridge-maintenance contract spanning a year is facilities'; a same-day call raised mid-service may be this row's only when the trading-floor urgency and site-day context are present.

AN EXTENSION OR SOURCE_TYPE alone - “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”

Membership in a download session that dropped a folder of store paperwork at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

work_types: labour plan against forecast trade - rota with covers or sales forecast, SPLH or labour-percentage column
opening checklist - trading-floor open acts with initials, keyed to site and date
closing checklist - trading-floor close acts with initials, keyed to site and date
shift handover note - trading-floor state passed between duty managers
brand standards or mystery-shopper visit scorecard - scored selling-space walk
reactive trading-floor incident call - same-day fault raised during service
site-day or site-week pack - assembled cover and contents binding the day's operating records
grouping_reasons: ONE SITE OPERATING DAY across its trail: the labour plan for that day, the opening check, the closing check, the handover notes, any standards visit that day, and any reactive call raised during it - joined by site identity and trading date, never by a staff name. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
ONE STANDARDS VISIT across its trail: the scorecard, the photographic evidence of the selling space, the action list and the follow-up tick - joined by visit reference or visit date at one site.

ONE SITE-WEEK PACK: the bound assembly whose contents page lists checks, rotas and visits for one site over one week - the pack is the group reason; contained Z-reads and food-safety sheets keep their own schema evidence and are not rewritten.
No group at all is a valid and common outcome. A lone blank checklist, a lone staff rota with no forecast column, or a lone maintenance contract has not demonstrated a site operating day.

template.why: Empty by contract: PR-6 leaves the `retail_hospitality` schema with no field rows, and a dimension may only branch on a field the same schema declares. THE RECOMMENDATION IS HELD AS PROSE, AND ITS DIFFERENCE FROM THE PARENT'S DEFAULT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR THIS ROW. The schema's default is: TRADING UNIT (site, venue or channel) where the corpus spans more than one, then TRADING OCCASION - named there as the session, count, order cycle, booking, function or licensed premises the material belongs to - then OPERATIONAL RECORD FUNCTION. This row recommends: TRADING UNIT, then THE SITE OPERATING DAY AS ITS OWN OCCASION, then function. The difference is at the OCCASION level. A site operating day is none of the parent's five enumerated shapes: a SESSION is a till close (`retail_hospitality.pos-reporting`); a COUNT is a stocktake; an ORDER CYCLE is supplier replenishment; a BOOKING or FUNCTION is capacity sold; a LICENSED PREMISES is the permission file. This occasion is bounded by OPEN AND CLOSE OF THE SELLING SPACE, centres on LABOUR CAPACITY PLANNED AGAINST FORECAST TRADE and the operative diary of the floor, and assembles checks, handovers and brand walks that no other sibling requires as a set. NOT TIME-FIRST: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” The trading date identifies the day; it does not root the tree. The photos exception does not apply: “Photos and capture-based media are the major exception: time often belongs first because capture date is a defining aspect of the material.” A STAFF NAME must never become a dimension. Any later order remains editable - “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Week 12 rota.xlsx` - names down the side, days across the top, hours in the cells. This row owns THE SHIFT AS A CAPACITY PLAN against forecast covers or sales, with a sales-per-labour-hour or labour-percentage column; hr owns THE EMPLOYEE schedule keyed to contracted hours, absence codes or pay rates. Discriminated by THE FORECAST-TRADE COLUMN: present, the sheet is this row's; absent and replaced by contracted-hours/absence/pay, it is hr's; absent entirely, neither row should activate on these bytes alone (NJ-SO-1 / parent NJ-RH-1). Reciprocal: THIS ROW MUST NOT TAKE a named employee's disciplinary file, training certificate or payroll register; HR MUST NOT TAKE the labour forecast, the opening-checks sheet, or a brand-standards scorecard merely because an operative signed it. falls_through_to.why: The primary fallthrough for this row's undecidable cases - the bare `Week 12 rota.xlsx` with no forecast column and no hr columns, a mixed clipboard whose probe rows and till rows cannot be separated, a Unit 4 opening-check sheet whose property-versus-trade vocabulary is unsettled. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The home for a durable standalone site document with no operating day around it - a single hygiene-rating certificate on the wall, a lone blank checklist template, a one-off licence copy filed without a pack. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The required home when store-ops material turns out to be a staff or public dossier rather than an operating record - CCTV of customers and staff with no accompanying checklist, a handover naming a guest allegation and a staff member, a labour plan used as a suspicion list. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.” Also: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

An isolated transactional document that only looks site-shaped - a lone contractor call-out invoice with no site-day context, a single purchase receipt for cleaning supplies. “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.”

A password-protected site-pack export or an unreadable rota binary. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: SAME VALUE AS THE FAMILY, DIFFERENT SUBJECT MIX, and the delta is what passes leg 3. The parent posture rests on volume of third-party guest data. This row's ordinary output is STAFF-FACING FIRST: labour plans naming employees, shift handovers naming duty managers, till-exception mentions that are allegation-adjacent, and reactive incident prose that often names both a guest and a staff member. It can ALSO carry guest-affecting material and - if NJ-SO-4 admits them - trading-floor CCTV images of the public. The posture is therefore potentially_sensitive because the family cannot separate safe checklists from named-person members at recognition time. It does not invent a handling class. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”
open_question: Five, recorded rather than smoothed. NJ-SO-1 (sharpest, inherits parent NJ-RH-1): the bare rota `Week 12 rota.xlsx` with names, days and hours is undecidable between this row and `hr` on its own bytes. Proposed discriminator: sales-per-labour-hour / labour-percentage / forecast-covers decides for this family; contracted-hours / absence / pay decides for hr; neither present means abstain. Alternative: hr takes every rota and this family takes only the trade forecast sheet it is built from. Both rows must say the same thing. NJ-SO-2: does the roster hint's 'compliance paperwork the site must hold' survive as a member of this row, or is every durable permission file `retail_hospitality.premises-licensing` / `retail_hospitality.food-safety` / Independent Records? This pass narrows to refuse the durable pack as a defining structure and keeps only the site-day diary - R1c should confirm. NJ-SO-3: is a brand-standards / mystery-shopper visit truly outside `business_operations.compliance-audit`, or does any scored third-party visit become an assessment occurrence? Alternatives: keep the brand/regulatory split (this pass); fold mystery shopper into compliance-audit and narrow this row to open/close + labour + handover only. NJ-SO-4: trading-floor CCTV and door-access media - inherits parent NJ-RH-4. Alternatives: admit under this row when paired with a site-day pack; privacy-only route to Protected Records with no domain claim (this pass's file-example posture); or a security world that does not yet exist. NJ-SO-5: should `trading_occasion` widen to admit SITE OPERATING DAY as a sixth shape beside session/count/order/booking/function/licence, or does this row need the day to remain prose-only until fields exist? Widening is preferred; minting `operating_day` would be a synonym.
